scripts/aacr-miss-anatomy.mjs: The readback that turns one benchmark artifact into the table the next device is chosen from: it splits the goldens we commented near and the judge rejected by whether our comment at that site was itself accepted. It buys nothing and calls nothing, so it is not a check that can go red - it is the reading a person does after a run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` now cites it instead of a hand count. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded.
scripts/extract-real-ground-truth.mjs: Rewrites the PR-review ground truth from public bug-fix commits, so running it inside a pull request would replace the dataset the pull request is being judged against. It needs the GitHub API and a judge model, and its output is committed deliberately. Local tool: run it when the dataset changes, not on every push.
scripts/measure-candidate.mjs: A developer's question — which tests name this file, and what do they say its coverage is — answered on demand for one path. It measures nothing on its own and borrows the run that is already happening, so a CI invocation would produce a figure about the file the workflow happened to be editing.
scripts/generate-comparison-report.ts: Runs the full CA-Bench industry comparison and writes docs/INDUSTRY_COMPARISON.md plus the dashboard. It is a document generator, not a check: wiring it today would either commit on every push or leave the document silently stale. Recorded in the roadmap as a generated-and-compared step, with the comparison and not the generation being the thing a gate can assert.
scripts/run-llm-bench.ts: A standalone DeepSeek review-quality benchmark needing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. The same protocol is scored inside the repository by the evaluation protocol scorers and by the Martian harness, both of which run in workflows and publish artifacts; this entry point exists for a single run against a candidate model, which is a person's decision rather than a nightly job.
scripts/code-scanning-corpus.mjs: Walks the open code-scanning corpus and prints the per-rule and per-path tables a triage has to start from. It is a reader of somebody else's measurement: the alerts are produced by CodeQL and Scorecard, and the count moves whenever one of their scans finishes, so a workflow that gated on it would go red for a rescan rather than for a change. It also needs `security-events: read`, which is a permission surface this repository has been narrowing rather than widening, and iteration 117 already removed four scheduled jobs that re-derived numbers nobody read. Local tool: run it when security work starts, which is what `docs/SECURITY.md` tells the next reader to do.
scripts/aacr-merge-slices.mjs: Merges the artifacts of two dispatches over disjoint slices into the two artifacts the comparison job reads, so that a registration naming both halves of a corpus is answered on two hundred rows instead of a hundred. It buys nothing and calls nothing, and its inputs are the artifacts of runs a person has already paid for, so a workflow that gated on it would be gating on artifacts that may not exist yet. Local tool: run it after the second slice lands, then feed both outputs to `aacr-ablation-compare.mjs`.
scripts/anchor-rate.mjs: The readback that turns one paid artifact into the four numbers R-41 was registered against - the anchoring rate, precision among anchored comments and among the rest, and the 2x2 - so that §91's table can be rebuilt after the code that produced it was reverted. It buys nothing and calls nothing: its input is an artifact a dispatch already paid for, and a workflow that gated on it would be gating on a file that only exists after somebody spends money. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded, which is what `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §91 did.
scripts/polyglot-scale.ts: The scanner measured over three hundred real files, judged by the same third-party grammars the polyglot bench uses. **It is a local tool and not a gate** because its corpus is whatever this machine has installed - `node_modules` and a Python tree - so a CI run would measure a different sample and post a number nobody registered. It bought the three defects of §92: a backtick that blanked four standard-library files, an oracle that could not see a declared function, and a recall that could exceed its own precision because a name was counted twice.
scripts/witness-replay.mjs: Replays a paid review artifact against the file each finding stands in, so the index's structural facts and cross-file facts (is the line inside a declaration, is the declaration one this diff touched, does the comment name a declared callee) can be scored as selectors without a model. It reads a committed artifact and the GitHub API, writes a new artifact and buys nothing, so it cannot go red - it is the reading a person does after a run. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded; its output is committed deliberately.
scripts/cross-file-report.mjs: Measures the cross-file index in `packages/intelligence/src/review/index/repo-index.ts` over this repository's own sources: how many relative imports resolve, how many names cross a file boundary, and whether `ts.resolveModuleName` agrees with every one of them. It reads local files, writes `benchmarks/cross-file-index.json` with `--json`, and makes no network call and no model call, so it cannot go red - it is the reading a person does when the resolver changes. Local tool: run it after editing the resolver and commit the artifact deliberately; the test that guards the resolver is `packages/intelligence/src/review/index/__tests__/a-change-crosses-files-and-the-index-has-to-say-where.test.ts`.
scripts/filter-ceiling.mjs: The readback that decides whether a fifth selection device is worth building: it computes, from the two artifacts already paid for, the best F1 any filter could reach on the findings this run produced and the precision-matched-goldens frontier a target of 0.4500 requires. It buys nothing, calls nothing and fetches nothing, so it cannot go red - it is the reading that four null devices needed and did not have, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §96 cites it instead of an argument.
scripts/import-oracle.ts: The second implementation of the import readers: it asks tree-sitter where each import statement is and what it names, for the five languages this repository has a grammar for and no compiler, and prints the multiset agreement per language. It cannot go red - it is the reading that found three defects and one wrong oracle rule on its first run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §97 cites it instead of an assertion.
scripts/budget-frontier.mjs: The readback that prices the per-pull-request budget: it re-ranks one paid run at eight budgets and prints matched goldens, F1, finding-text characters and the marginal goldens per thousand tokens, so the budget is chosen as a purchase rather than by F1 alone. It buys nothing, calls nothing and fetches nothing, so it cannot go red - `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §99 cites it instead of an argument about diminishing returns.
scripts/corpus-index-report.mjs: Measures what the index can say in a checkout it did not write, by language: files, declarations, import statements, the four refusals, the edges that cross, and what a reach note for the whole repository would cost a prompt. **It is a local tool and not a gate** because its input is any repository on disk - twelve of them were measured for §115 at named commits and the artifact records the commits - so a CI run would either need seven clones or measure whatever happened to be present, and a number nobody registered is worse than no number. It reads local files, writes `benchmarks/polyglot-index.json` with `--json`, and makes no network call and no model call. Local tool: run it against a checkout when the readers change and commit the artifact deliberately; the reader itself is guarded by `packages/intelligence/src/review/index/__tests__/` and its statement set is judged by `scripts/import-oracle.ts`, and the artifact's shape is guarded by `tests/unit/scripts/a-language-with-a-denominator-is-a-repository.test.ts` - which fails on a subtree published as a repository, a row with no commit, a row whose language counts do not add up to its own totals, and a JavaScript or TypeScript denominator below the floor §115.4 established.
scripts/selection-audit.mjs: The readback that asks whether the cut a campaign ships was chosen by the corpus it is scored on: it leaves one pull request out at a time, chooses the knob on the other forty-nine and applies that choice to the one held out. It buys nothing and calls nothing, so it is not a check that can go red - it is the reading a person does after a run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §108 is the reading it produced. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded; the numbers it prints go into the section that quotes them.
scripts/ranker-replay.mjs: The readback that asks whether a fitted ordering beats the weights already in the tree: it applies the shipped cut and the corpus's own maximum matching to one artifact's rows, with `score` replaced by a leave-one-pull-request-out prediction over the eight engine-side features, and prints the budget curve beside it. It buys nothing and calls nothing, so it is not a check that can go red - it is the reading a person does after a run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §113 is what it produced. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded; every number it prints is reproducible from that file alone.
scripts/compare-spend.mjs: The readback that makes a cost clause readable at all: it prints two artifacts' bills in four units - billed USD, cold-cache USD, prompt tokens, calls - and says whether the billed and cold-cache figures agree about the direction, because the vendor's prefix cache outlives the process and the arm that runs second is billed less for the same tokens (2026-11-21: the arm with one fewer lane out of five was billed 10.5 % more, on 82.9 % cache hits against 51.0 %). It buys nothing and calls nothing and its multiplier is recovered from each arm's own bill rather than assumed, so it is not a check that can go red - it is the reading a person does after a run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §117 is the reading it produced. Local tool: run it on the two artifacts you just downloaded.
scripts/cost-unit-figure.mjs: The figure generator for the cost pair: it reads two artifacts and draws what the account was charged beside what the same tokens would have cost on a cold cache, with the two ratios printed under each group and the cache hit shares under the axis. It is a local tool rather than a gate because it needs the two artifacts, which are a run's outputs and not the repository's - but `--check` compares the file it would write with the file in the tree, so once a figure is committed a stale one is a command that exits non-zero rather than a picture nobody notices. `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §117.7 is the section it draws.
scripts/judge-pair-anatomy.mjs: The readback that prices the cheapest-looking alternative to R-56 before it is registered: it applies five rules over the judge's `(finding path, golden path)` pairs, re-scores each surviving pool, and prints the evaluation column beside the product column. On the five-lane arm of 44867457528 the strictest rule keeps 13.09 % of the pairs and costs 0.0431 of F1, so the filter is a loss and the batch is the only remaining lever. Local tool: it needs an artifact and a corpus file, buys nothing, and calls nothing.
scripts/judge-batch-arithmetic.mjs: The arithmetic a batched judge arm is registered on: `buildJudgeMessages` is pure, so the length of every request the judge would receive is computable from an artifact and a corpus file with no model involved. It reports requests and prompt characters per batch size, and the mean system prefix against the vendor's 64-token cache block - 712 characters, about 178 tokens, which is the measurement that shows §110's premise about a shared block that does not exist to be wrong. Local tool: needs one artifact and one corpus file.
scripts/recall-ceiling-figure.mjs: The figure generator for the recall ceiling: it reads benchmarks/recall-ceiling.json - the four-way split of R-55's 330 goldens into emitted, budget-blocked, rule-dropped and absent - and draws one stacked bar whose last segment is the 68.5 % no device in this repository can move. It is a local tool rather than a gate because the split comes from a run's artifact, which is not the repository's; but `--check` compares the file it would write with the file in the tree, so a committed figure gone stale is a command that exits non-zero rather than a picture nobody notices. `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §124.1 is the section it draws, and `checkStages` refuses to draw at all when the four segments do not sum to the corpus.
scripts/gate-replay.mjs: The readback that prices the grounding gate on a paid artifact's own removals: it applies `decideGrounding` in front of the shipped cut, per pull request, against the file each finding stands in at the head commit the run read, and prints the two points, the share of the removals that were true positives, the goldens lost and gained, and the pull requests whose gate was withheld. It buys nothing and calls no model - two API reads per pull request and one raw read per file, cached and pinned to the commit it records - so it cannot go red; `--check` re-runs the arithmetic against a committed output and exits non-zero when the figure moved. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded, which is what `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §149 did. The arithmetic is guarded by `tests/unit/scripts/a-grounding-gate-is-priced-on-the-files-it-read.test.ts`.
scripts/harvest-changed-lines.mjs: The one input §169 could not take from the tree: the identifiers each pull request's own added lines write. It needs fifty GitHub diff requests, so a gate that ran it would go red on a rate limit rather than on a change, and its result is a property of the pull requests at the moment they were read - which is why the file it writes is committed and why `bench:symbol-adjacency` reads that file instead of fetching. The record it produced is held to the corpus by `tests/unit/scripts/the-harvest-covers-the-corpus-it-claims.test.ts`, which recomputes sha256 of the corpus bytes and requires the harvest to name them - so a corpus that moved without a re-harvest fails a test rather than quietly pricing §166's prize on the old names. Local tool: run `npm run bench:changed-lines` when the corpus changes, and commit the artifact deliberately.
